comments.author: @wilhelmhesse1348
comments.text:
Thanks and great advice but you missed one key point, a patent does have loopholes and just showing the invention to a distributor or manufacturer after failing to come up to an agreement, should they be very interested in the idea could lead to them designing something similar but not the same. 

The distributor/ manufacturer has the means, the money, the patent  lawyers, the resources to beat me in their sleep and some how get their way. 

I would strongly advise against approaching distributors/ manufacturers with just designs and a registered patent on paper but rather  develop the product fully and create your own company. Then market and sell the two, the firm and the intellectual property. 

My two cents.

Hi John,
Great video which I just now discovered!  One thing that would also be helpful to address is the possibility of patent infringement.  Even if you do a patent search, there is no guarantee that there isn’t prior art out there or is lurking in the 18-month “black hole” between an application filed and publication.  Consequently, how is the possibility of patent infringement handled in negotiating a licensing agreement?  This would be bad news if the licensee invested in manufacturing and I as the licensor would not want to be exposed to damages incurred by the licensee.  😮Thanks!
